address_english: Standalone annex buildings attached to district courts at all court locations across Egypt
notable_notes: Under Law No. 10 of 2004, every district court (Mahkama Juz'iyya) in Egypt must have an attached Family Court annex. As of 2024, there are over 250 Family Court buildings/annexes across Egypt. An Office of Family Dispute Settlement (مكتب تسوية المنازعات الأسرية) is mandatory at each, providing mediation before filing. Christian personal status matters are handled by separate Coptic and Evangelical ecclesiastical councils, not civil family courts.
audit_notes: Consolidated entry added during completeness audit to represent the full nationwide family court network beyond entries already individually listed.

notable_notes: Egypt's military judiciary operates courts corresponding to the Army's five regional commands: Northern Command (Alexandria), Central Command (Cairo), Southern Command (Assiut), Eastern Command (Ismailia/Canal Zone), and Western Command (Marsa Matrouh). Each command has first-instance and appeals-level military courts. Under Law No. 25/1966 as amended by Law No. 16/2007.
confidence_note: The five-command structure is publicly documented; precise addresses, phone numbers, and operational details of individual military courts are classified and not available in open sources.
